issues.legal_issue: Foreign creditors may prove their claims in a local winding up of a foreign-incorporated company as an unregistered company, without showing that their debts arose from the company’s local business.
material_facts: The company was incorporated abroad and carried on business in India before ceasing that business.
The company was being wound up in India as an unregistered company, and the liquidator had collected assets there.
Foreign creditors submitted proofs of debts owed by the company.
The appellant objected that the proceedings were only for Indian creditors and that foreign creditors’ debts had to relate to the company’s Indian business.
issues.conclusion: Foreign creditors could prove their claims in the winding up, and their claims were not restricted to debts connected with the company’s Indian business.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 270–276 of the Indian Companies Act, 1913 govern winding up of unregistered companies. Section 271(1) applies the Act’s winding-up provisions subject to specified exceptions and additions, and section 271(3) permits a foreign-incorporated company that has carried on business in India to be wound up as an unregistered company when it ceases that business. Sections 272, 156, 158, 166 and 167 make no relevant distinction between Indian and foreign creditors or contributories; section 167 makes a winding-up order operate for all creditors and contributories. Section 211 provides for pari passu application of company property to liabilities, and section 228 admits all debts and claims against the company to proof. A local winding up is ancillary to the winding up in the company’s country of incorporation, but concerns the same company and its creditors, not a separate local entity. The Court relied on In re Commercial Bank of South Australia, L.R. [1886] 33 Ch. D. 174; In re Hibernian Merchants Ltd., L.R. [1958] 1 Ch. D. 76; In re English, Scottish, and Australian Chartered Bank, L.R. [1893] 3 Ch. D. 385; Russian and English Bank v. Baring Bros., [1936] 1 All E.R. 505; and Re Azoff-Don Commercial Bank, [1954] 1 All E.R. 947, in support of the ancillary character of local proceedings and distribution for the whole body of creditors.

predicates.local_unregistered_company_winding_up: A court is winding up in its jurisdiction, as an unregistered company, a company incorporated elsewhere that carried on business there.
predicates.foreign_creditors_are_creditors_of_same_: Creditors located abroad hold claims against the same company being wound up, rather than against a separate local entity.
predicates.company_has_assets_within_local_jurisdic: The company has assets within the jurisdiction in which the winding-up proceeding is conducted.

issues.definition: When a local court winds up a foreign-incorporated company as an unregistered company, foreign creditors of that same company may prove their claims against its assets within the jurisdiction.
